_about: Catalog of long-running physical-layer series for the history layer: energy, emissions, resources, land, technology diffusion. Status: pulled = in this directory; planned = retrievable by URL in the workflow; attach = the file must be supplied (login or no stable URL). Every pulled series records its source commit or retrieval date and license. Feeds = the derived feature it supports.

entries.title: Fossil CO2 emissions by country, annual (Global Carbon Budget via Our World in Data)
entries.retrieval: shallow clone of github.com/owid/co2-data (commit in owid_extract.provenance.json)
entries.license: OWID processing CC BY 4.0; Global Carbon Budget CC BY 4.0
entries.caveat: a proxy for fossil energy use; drifts with efficiency and decarbonization, hence the trailing-10-year anomaly

entries.title: Primary energy consumption, fossil production and consumption by fuel, electricity generation (EIA, Energy Institute, Ember via Our World in Data)
entries.coverage: 18 JST countries; consumption 1965-2024, production 1900-2024 for most
entries.license: OWID CC BY 4.0; EIA public domain; Energy Institute Statistical Review free with attribution; Ember CC BY 4.0

entries.title: Crude oil prices since 1861 (Energy Institute Statistical Review; also served by Our World in Data's grapher)
entries.retrieval: workflow: ourworldindata.org/grapher/crude-oil-prices CSV export (manifest.json has URL, hash, time)
entries.note: the supply-shock channel; FRED WTISPLC covers 1946- in the meantime

entries.title: Spot crude oil price, WTI, monthly 1946- (FRED)
feeds: (not yet used: the 1861- series covers it; kept for the bridge)

entries.title: Producer price index, all commodities, monthly 1913- (FRED)
entries.retrieval: workflow: FRED API (history/physical/raw/FRED-PHYSICAL/PPIACO.csv, monthly, averaged to years)

entries.title: US primary energy consumption by source, annual 1949- (EIA Total Energy API: total, coal, petroleum, natural gas, nuclear, renewables; trillion Btu)
entries.retrieval: workflow: api.eia.gov/v2/total-energy with the EIA_API_KEY secret (history/physical/raw/EIA-TOTAL-ENERGY/us_primary_energy_annual.csv; manifest.json has URL, hash, time); eia_extract.csv is the tidy table with fossil share and growth
feeds: energy_growth_3y, energy_gap_3y for the US 1952-1967 (energy_src = eia), where OWID's series has no value
fossil_share (eia_extract.csv), for a measured fuel mix beside the CO2-based shares
entries.note: the 1635-1945 estimated-consumption table is queued as EIA-HISTORICAL-1635

entries.title: Estimated US energy consumption by source for selected years 1635-1945 (EIA Energy Explained table: wood, coal, petroleum, natural gas, hydro)
entries.coverage: US, 42 selected years: 1635-1845 every ten years (wood only), 1850-1945 every five years (coal, gas, petroleum, hydro, wood, net electricity imports); quadrillion Btu
entries.retrieval: workflow: the notes page (HTML) and the table (PDF) under history/physical/raw/EIA-HISTORICAL-1635/; tools/eia_hist_parse.py reads the PDF's text layer into eia_1635_1945.csv with every row's sums checked
feeds: calibration of the CO2 proxy: CO2 growth tracks fossil energy growth (corr 0.99) but overstates total energy growth by 4.5 pp/yr before 1900 while wood was being displaced; the footprint gap's trailing anomaly, not its raw level, is the pre-1900 feature
wood share of US energy (0.91 in 1850, 0.22 in 1900, 0.04 in 1945): the first energy transition
entries.caveat: five-year steps, so no 3-year growth; wood through 1945 is fuelwood only (series break at 1949); (s) = under 0.5 trillion Btu is written as 0; coverage follows settlement, not statehood (see the notes page)

entries.title: Energy consumption of European economies 1800-2008 (Kander, Malanima, Warde, Power to the People)
entries.coverage: about eight European countries incl. GBR, DEU, FRA, ITA, ESP, PRT, NLD, SWE
entries.retrieval: dataset distributed with the book / the Energy History project; supply the file
entries.note: replaces the CO2 proxy with measured consumption for the pre-1965 decades

entries.title: Cross-country Historical Adoption of Technology (Comin and Hobijn), 100+ technologies, 150 countries, 1750-2000
entries.coverage: 18 JST countries x 16 technologies used (rail km, telegrams, telephones, electricity, cars, commercial vehicles, radios, TVs, mail, aviation pkm, ship tonnage, tractors, fertilizer, cellphones, computers, internet users); most series end 1993-2003
entries.retrieval: workflow: NBER data appendix data.nber.org/data-appendix/w15319/ (FinalCHAT_72909.csv, chat.dta, README.TXT; manifest.json has URL, hash, time)
entries.license: NBER research data; free for research
entries.note: the diffusion channel: capacity outrunning demand near the inflection (1873, 1893, 2001); per-capita log growth from the latest observation in [t-5, t-2], post-inception only, no growth across one-year log jumps > 1 (108 flagged unit/territory breaks); nothing after 2003

entries.title: Real commodity prices 1850-2015, 40 commodities (Jacks 2013, 'From boom to bust')
entries.retrieval: author's data appendix; supply the file

entries.title: USGS historical statistics for mineral and material commodities (production, prices, since 1900)
entries.coverage: US production, imports, exports, apparent consumption, unit value nominal and real (98$/t), world production; 1900-2021/22; basket used: copper, lead, zinc, tin, nickel, aluminum, iron ore (+ pig iron world production, gold)
entries.retrieval: workflow: USGS series index -> 85 commodity workbooks (history/physical/raw/USGS-DS140/, manifest.json has URL, hash, time)
entries.note: global at t (the same for every country); prices are annual averages in US dollars, deflated by USGS with the US CPI

entries.title: Ore-grade decline compilations (Mudd and others: copper, gold)
entries.coverage: selected countries and global, decadal to annual
feeds: marginal_cost_proxy (slow variable for the long cycle)

entries.title: Residential land price series for six countries (No Price Like Home appendix, Figure 16)
entries.coverage: AUS BEL CHE GBR JPN USA
entries.retrieval: already encoded in history/jst/house_prices_documentation.md as figures; digitizing needs the authors' data
entries.note: JST's housing_rent_yd is the live land-scarcity valuation gauge meanwhile
